findings.description: The declared adoption payload still invokes Git without disabling core.fsmonitor. Its ls-files inventory can execute a repository-configured fsmonitor hook, violating the no-repository-code-execution contract. The proposed aidd_graphs.py has the same omission. Active sources include core.fsmonitor=false, but context-lock.json and verification-receipt.json still pin the older payload, so adopting those pinned files would remove this protection.
findings.recommendation: Update both proposed source pairs and their declared pins to preserve the fsmonitor protection.

findings.description: Saved security evidence does not establish coverage of the current source. The receipt pins code_graph.py to bceaf0f8..., aidd_graphs.py to 8519b558..., and the raw-hash tests to 22f9413c...; inspected active hashes are bcfeb0a7..., 1293eeb3..., and 1b359a7a.... These are substantive differences: active sources add fsmonitor protection and active tests add two fsmonitor cases. V-GR1-GREEN.log records only the earlier four tests. No listed execution evidence verifies the added cases against the current bytes. No tests were run during this review.
findings.recommendation: Provide execution evidence bound to the current source, mirrors, tests, and dependency identities.
